title: Phulera Is Coming Back, and This Time the Bad Guy Is in Charge: 'Panchayat' Season 5 Promises Something "Alag, Hatke"
excerpt: Banrakas has the council. Binod is being lifted on shoulders. And the cast just told a room full of people that the gentlest show on Indian streaming is about to get its sharpest twist yet.
body:
For six years, **Panchayat** has been the show you put on when the world is too loud. A sleepy little Prime Video series about an engineering graduate stuck in a dusty UP village office, it built a global cult not by raising the stakes but by lowering them — a missing CCTV camera, a solar panel, a love story conducted entirely in glances across a panchayat bhavan. Now its own cast is warning you that the calm is over.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=k_Wxtau_f04</youtube>

At a recent summit, three of the show's most beloved faces — **Durgesh Kumar** (the gloriously scheming Banrakas), **Sunita Rajwar** (the fearsome Kranti Devi) and **Ashok Pathak** (Binod, the breakout darling of Season 4) — sat down to tease the long-awaited fifth chapter. They gave away almost nothing. Which is, of course, exactly how Phulera likes it.

> "Aise toh nahin bata sakte, warna audience ka comic timing kharaab ho jaayega. Lekin, iss baar bhi anand aane waala hai." — Durgesh Kumar (Banrakas)

Translation, roughly: *I can't tell you, or I'll ruin the audience's comic timing. But this time too, it's going to be a joy.* Pathak, ever the showman, went a step further. "Mazza aayega," he promised. "Is baar ka season kuch alag, hatke hoga. Romaanch zyaada hone waala hai." *It'll be fun. This season will be different, off-beat. There'll be more thrill.*

That word — *romaanch*, thrill — is the tell. Because Season 4 ended on the franchise's most charged note yet. The former opposition clawed back power, leaving Banrakas's faction holding the village council after defeating Brij Bhushan and Manju Devi. The identity of Phulera's next Up-Pradhan is still a mystery. For the first time, the people we've spent four seasons rooting for are on the back foot, and the man we've spent four seasons laughing at is holding the gavel.

It's a genuinely clever place to leave a comfort-watch. The pleasure of **Panchayat** has always been its decency — Abhishek (**Jitendra Kumar**), Pradhan-pati Brij Bhushan (**Raghubir Yadav**), Manju Devi (**Neena Gupta**), Vikas (**Chandan Roy**), Prahlad (**Faisal Malik**), and the quietly blooming Rinki (**Sanvikaa**) — a found family you trust. Hand the keys to Banrakas and that decency suddenly has something to lose. The show that never needed a villain has finally let one win.

There is a real question hanging over all this, and the cast knows it. Season 4 drew the franchise's biggest opening but its most middling reviews; even admirers admitted the quirks were starting to feel like formula, the organic charm hardening into a packaged product. "Alag, hatke" isn't just a tease — it's a promise to people who worried Phulera had run out of road. Created by **Deepak Kumar Mishra** and written by **Chandan Kumar** under Arunabh Kumar's **The Viral Fever (TVF)**, the new season is built to answer that doubt.

For the diaspora, **Panchayat** has become something close to a homesickness cure. It streams worldwide on **Prime Video** — no separate window, no regional lock — which means an NRI in New Jersey or Leicester or Brampton can drop into Phulera the same day as a viewer in Lucknow. Prime Video India's own executives have marvelled at how the show travels: a series with no glamour, no spectacle, no stars in the conventional sense, somehow connecting with people who haven't lived in a village in a generation, or ever. It works precisely *because* it's small. The wedding you missed, the chaachi you only see on video calls, the slow rhythm of a place that doesn't rush — it's all in there.

No firm date yet, beyond the confirmed 2026 window, and TVF is keeping the premiere card close. Filming wrapped its key stretch earlier this year, and the marketing machine is clearly warming up — Banrakas talking to the press is itself a sign the campaign has begun. There's even been a viral detour into the real world: a clip of **PM Narendra Modi** meeting Pathak and Durgesh Kumar, "Binod se kuch baatein," did the rounds online, proof that a fictional UP village now commands the kind of attention reserved for actual statecraft.

So: Phulera is returning, the villain's in the chair, and the people who make it are grinning and refusing to explain why. After four seasons of teaching us to find drama in a solar lamp, **Panchayat** is betting it can find it in a coup. We'd watch Binod read a phone book. This should be easy.
